title: Management of Time and Energy

Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has four statements or pairs of ½ mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or arrange in sequence).

questions.q: State True or False: (i) All similar plates, katories and spoons should be washed together. (ii) The size of the family influences family expenditure. (iii) Budgeting helps to balance income and expenses. (iv) Time spent on rest and leisure is called peak load period.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) True. (iii) True. (iv) False – it is the leisure period.

questions.q: State True or False: (i) All activities should be listed before time planning. (ii) Shopping is an inflexible activity. (iii) Balancing is adjustment of time for each activity. (iv) A time plan should not be changed.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) False – shopping is flexible. (iii) True. (iv) False – a time plan should be flexible.

questions.q: State True or False: (i) Watching a television show is an inflexible activity. (ii) Working in a correct posture helps to save time. (iii) Doing two or more activities at the same time is called dovetailing. (iv) Washing bedsheets by hand is a heavy household activity.
questions.answer: (i) False – it is flexible. (ii) True. (iii) True. (iv) True.

questions.q: State True or False: (i) A time schedule should be flexible. (ii) Inflexible activities cannot be changed. (iii) Reducing time for some activities cannot help in balancing the time plan. (iv) It is important to correctly estimate the time required for each activity.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) True. (iii) False – reducing time on some activities helps balancing. (iv) True.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) When a number of activities are performed within a fixed time it is known as ______. (ii) A mixer is a ______ device. (iii) Two types of fatigue are ______ and ______.
questions.answer: (i) peak load. (ii) labour-saving. (iii) physical; mental.

questions.q: Classify as heavy, moderate or light work: (i) Preparing notes (ii) Mopping the house (iii) Cycling (iv) Listening to the radio.
questions.answer: (i) Moderate. (ii) Heavy. (iii) Heavy. (iv) Light.

questions.q: Arrange in the correct order for cleaning and rearranging a house: dusting, shifting the furniture, clearing webs, mopping, sweeping.
questions.answer: Shift the furniture, clear cobwebs, sweep, dust, mop.

questions.q: State True or False: (i) Time and energy are closely related. (ii) Time can be used more effectively without a time plan. (iii) Combining two or three activities is dovetailing. (iv) The number of activities need not be considered while making a time plan.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) False. (iii) True. (iv) False.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Write four steps of making a time plan.
questions.answer: (1) List all the activities. (2) Group them into flexible and inflexible activities. (3) Estimate the time required for each activity. (4) Balance – adjust the time of activities so that the total fits within the available time.

questions.q: Give any four suggestions to smoothly carry out household activities at home.
questions.answer: Make a time plan; break big tasks into smaller activities; cut unnecessary movements by carrying things together on a tray; do activities in the right order; use the correct posture; keep things near the place of use and put them back; use labour-saving devices; share work among family members.

questions.q: Explain the terms 'peak load' and 'dovetailing' with one example each.
questions.answer: Peak load: a period in the day when many activities must be done in a fixed time, e.g. the morning rush to get children ready for school. Dovetailing: doing two or more activities at the same time, e.g. putting dal on the stove and washing clothes in the machine while cutting vegetables.

questions.q: List any four household activities that are done every day.
questions.answer: Sweeping and mopping, dusting, cooking meals, washing dishes, making beds, tidying rooms, washing clothes.

questions.q: Give any four examples of cutting unnecessary movements to save energy.
questions.answer: Carry all glasses on a tray to serve guests; take the clothes and sweeping tools to the roof in one trip; clear the table in one or two trips by stacking plates; keep books near the study table; gather all ingredients before cooking.

questions.q: Mention any two heavy and two light household activities done by your mother.
questions.answer: Heavy: mopping the floor, washing clothes by hand, Diwali cleaning. Light: reading, telling a story, listening to the radio, preparing notes.

questions.q: Your brother gets tired while cleaning his room. Tell him four ways by which he gets tired.
questions.answer: Working in a wrong posture (bending for long); making unnecessary movements; doing activities in the wrong order (dusting before sweeping); working at an uncomfortable height; keeping things far away; not taking rest or breaking the task into parts.

questions.q: By dovetailing, the work of cooking dal, cooking vegetables, washing dishes and washing clothes (20 minutes each) was finished in 55 minutes. How much time was saved?
questions.answer: Without dovetailing: 20 + 20 + 20 + 20 = 80 minutes. With dovetailing: 55 minutes. Time saved = 80 – 55 = 25 minutes.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Many household activities can be avoided to save energy. Identify any three such activities. Give one suggestion each to improve these.
questions.answer: (1) Going to the kitchen again and again to bring things – put all items on a tray and bring them in one trip. (2) Bending to sweep with a short broom – use a long-handled broom. (3) Searching for things – keep things at their places near where they are used. (4) Ironing or cooking at a wrong height – raise the working surface to a comfortable height.

questions.q: Your sister complains of backache. Give her any six suggestions to save energy while doing household chores.
questions.answer: Sit or stand erect and do not bend for long; use a long-handled broom and mop; work at a comfortable height (ironing table, kitchen counter); keep things near the place of use; break the task into smaller activities with rests in between; use labour-saving devices like a mixer; dovetail activities and share work with family members.

questions.q: Identify any three bad postures of your mother while doing household chores. Suggest one way in each case to improve them.
questions.answer: (1) Bending to sweep with a short broom – use a long-handled broom. (2) Sitting on the floor to iron or cook – work at a table or counter of comfortable height. (3) Stretching up to reach things stored too high – keep things within easy reach near the place of use.

questions.q: Your family is always short of time. Tell your family members six benefits of making a time plan.
questions.answer: You finish work efficiently without feeling tired; get time for rest; get time for hobbies; do more productive work in less time; are saved from last-minute tension and confusion; get time for unforeseen events like guests or illness; the quality of work improves.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the steps in making a time plan and how dovetailing helps to save time.
questions.answer: Steps: list all the activities; group them as flexible (shopping) and inflexible (school, classes); estimate the time for each; balance the time by reducing time on some activities so the total fits within 24 hours. A good plan is practical and flexible, has an alternative for emergencies and allows rest and leisure. Dovetailing means doing two or three activities together: cooking dal, cooking vegetables, washing dishes and washing clothes take 80 minutes separately but only 55 minutes when dovetailed (starting the washing machine, boiling dal, cutting vegetables meanwhile), saving 25 minutes.

questions.q: Describe five ways of saving energy while doing household activities.
questions.answer: (1) Break the task into smaller activities (washing clothes: sort, soak, rub, rinse, dry). (2) Cut extra movements and combine activities (serve glasses on a tray). (3) Do activities in the proper order (sweep before dusting is wrong – dust first, then sweep). (4) Be skilled and use the correct posture (long-handled broom, sit erect). (5) Work at proper heights and keep things near the place of use. (6) Use labour-saving devices such as a mixer grinder.
